SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY.
N. D - 30 /
Date 1 / 4 / 33

April 24 33

Dear Barton,

With reference to your letter of April 1, 1933,
forwarding copies of two Japanese handbills, I have to
inform you that neither of these leaflets was found during
the course of our recent raids on Communist bases. Both
these handbills are on file in this office, one being
obtained in the Hongkew area on January 9, 1933 and the
other found in the Eastern District on February 20, 1933.
According to our information these handbills were written
by one K. Fukuda, a student of the Tung Wen College. Fukuda
was arrested on March 1, 1933, on information supplied by
T. Sakamaki, a Japanese Communist who was arrested by the
Municipal Police on March 11, 1933.

The two Japanese handbills are returned herewith.

Yours sincerely

J. Barton, Esq.,
British Consulate-General.

Made by and Forwarded by J B Km

With reference to the letter dated 21.4.33 from H.B.M.
Consul-General forwarding two samples of propaganda leaflets
distributed amongst Japanese troops here, I have to report that
the leaflets in question are only copies and that the originals
are to be found on file D.4301, which is attached herewith.

of our recent raids on communist bases. According to
information obtained by D.S. Umemoto from the Japanese Consular
Authorities the leaflets were written by one K. Fukuda, a
student of the Tung Wen College, who was arrested on March 12,
1933, on information supplied by T. Sakamaki who forms the

Memorandum on a Japanese Communist named T. Sakamaki and ~~and~~ the
circumstances leading up to his arrest.

Towards the end of last year signs were not wanting that
the Shanghai Korean branch of/the Chinese Communist Party had
recovered from/ its inertia and was again showing renewed
activity.

An item appeared in the Shanghai Nich-Nichi newspaper
stating that on November 29 and 30 a number of communistic hand-
bills containing the exhortation "Smash the ~~anti-imperialist~~ anti-
communist propaganda of the Imperialists" was distributed in
cafes and restaurants in the Hongkew district frequented by
Japanese marines. According to the "Nichi-Nichi", these particular
pamphlets were issued by a committee formed by the Shanghai
Korean branch of the Chinese Communist Party.

Soon after the publication of the article in question
enquiries were instituted by the Special Branch of the Shanghai
Municipal Police, but although the cafes and restaurants mentioned
were visited and the proprietors of the same questioned, no
confirmation that communistic handbills had been distributed
could be obtained.

On January 9, 1933 information was received that a Japanese
military intelligence officer had discovered that morning pasted
upon benches near the bandstand in Hongkew Park several copies
of subversive handbills drawn up in Japanese. These handbills
bore as title the following slogan :"We oppose discriminating
Treatment", and were apparently the work of the "Third Fleet
Sailors Conference".

The next phase in the distribution of subversive Japanese
literature was the alleged attempt to conceal reactionary
pamphlets in matchboxes. A Mr. Nishioka alias Kitaoka, proprietor
of the Nishioka Restaurant, 83 Woosung Road, reported to the
Municipal Police that on January 20 he purchased a package of
matches containing ten boxes from a general store in Woosung Road.
On January 29 he discovered, so he states, two copies of commun-
istic pamphlets which were neatly folded and hidden under the

关于一名名为 T. Sakamaki 的日本共产党员及其被捕经过的备忘录。

去年年底，种种迹象表明，中国共产党上海朝鲜支部已从停滞状态中恢复，并再次显示出新的活动迹象。

《上海日日新闻》刊登了一则消息，称11月29日和30日，一些含有“粉碎帝国主义者的~~反帝国主义~~反共宣传”口号的共产主义传单，在虹口区日本海军陆战队常去的咖啡馆和餐馆中分发。据《日日新闻》称，这些特定的小册子是由中国共产党上海朝鲜支部成立的一个委员会发行的。

在该文章发表后不久，上海公共租界工部局警务处特别股展开了调查，尽管走访了提到的咖啡馆和餐馆并询问了业主，但未能获得确证证明曾分发过共产主义传单。

1933年1月9日，收到情报称，一名日本军事情报官员当天早晨在虹口公园乐队台附近的长椅上发现张贴着几份用日文撰写的颠覆性传单。这些传单的标题为以下标语：“我们反对歧视性待遇”，显然是“第三舰队水兵会议”的作品。

分发颠覆性日本文献的下一阶段是据称试图将反动小册子藏在火柴盒中。吴淞路83号西冈餐厅（Nishioka Restaurant）的老板西冈（Nishioka），又名北冈（Kitaoka），向工部局警务处报告称，1月20日他从吴淞路的一家杂货店购买了一包包含十盒的火柴。1月29日，他发现（据他陈述）两份折叠整齐并藏在

page_data.en:
(2)

matches in one of the boxes. A search of the contents of the
other match boxes led to the discovery of one more communistic
pamphlet which, like the others, was an appeal to Japanese sail-
ors to oppose the so-called capitalists and imperialists war
and to refrain from killing Chinese brethren. It winds up by
urging them to join the Sailors' Kyogikai.

The theory put forward by Nishioka is that some person who
was aware that he purchased matches for sale in the restaurant
placed the pamphlets in the match-boxes, thinking that by this
means they would come into the possession of the Japanese sailors
who use this restaurant.

The only other instance on record of finding communistic
matter in match boxes was reported by a Japanese sailor, who
alleged that he found a reactionary handbill inside a match-box
which he picked up inside the compound of the Japanese Naval
Club in Woosung Road on January 24.

On February 23 a communistic handbill in Japanese was
obtained by an agent of the S.M. Police in Western Chapei. This
pamphlet, which was published by the Youth Section of the Third
Fleet Sailors Conference, urges Japanese sailors to demand a 100%
increase in pay ; to demand to be sent home, and to lend
assistance to the above communist organisation.

At 7.30 p.m. on March 11 the Municipal Police, acting under
the authority of a warrant issued by the Japanese Consulate-
General, conducted a raid at the Tai Ping Yang (    ) Hotel,
430 Kwangsi Road, and in Room 62 arrested a Japanese communist
named T. Sakamaki alias Yamamoto, on a charge of violation of the
Peace Preservation Law of Japan. The accused after interrogation
was handed over to the Japanese Consular Police. A Chinese named
                                          Palikao
Wang Nai An (    ), owner of a fruit stall at 115 Rue □□
□□□□, found in the room at the time of the visit, was also
taken into custody. The latter is now being held on a writ of
detention, there being reasons to believe that he was employed as
liaison officer between the Japanese and Chinese Communist Parties.

(2)

其中一个盒子火柴下面的共产主义小册子。对其他火柴盒内容的搜查导致又发现了一份共产主义小册子，与其他小册子一样，它呼吁日本水兵反对所谓的资本家和帝国主义战争，并 refrain from killing Chinese brethren（避免杀害中国兄弟）。最后敦促他们加入水兵协谊会（Sailors' Kyogikai）。

西冈提出的理论是，某个知道他购买火柴用于餐厅销售的人，将小册子放入火柴盒中，认为通过这种方式，它们会落入使用这家餐厅的日本水兵手中。

记录在案的另一起在火柴盒中发现共产主义材料的案例是由一名日本水兵报告的，他声称1月24日在吴淞路日本海军俱乐部大院里捡到的一个火柴盒内发现了一份反动传单。

2月23日，工部局警务处的一名特工在闸北西区获得了一份日文共产主义传单。这本由第三舰队水兵会议青年部出版的小册子，敦促日本水兵要求加薪100%；要求被送回国，并向上述共产主义组织提供援助。

3月11日晚上7点30分，工部局警务处根据日本总领事馆签发的搜查令，对广西路430号太平洋（Tai Ping Yang）酒店进行了突击搜查，并在62号房间逮捕了一名名为 T. Sakamaki，又名山本（Yamamoto）的日本共产党员，指控其违反日本《治安维持法》。被告经审讯后被移交给日本领事警察。一名中文名为王乃安（Wang Nai An）（音译：Palikao）的中国人，系□□路115号水果摊主，在搜查时被发现位于该房间内，也被拘留。后者目前正凭拘留令被羁押，因为有理由相信他被雇为日本共产党与中国共产党之间的联络官。

page_data.en:
(3)

A few days after these arrests had been effected
information indicating that Sakamaki was the author of the
communist handbills in the Japanese language issued by the "Youth
Section of the Third Fleet Sailors Conference was received from
the local Japanese Consular Police. Several copies of these
handbills, be it noted, have been found recently in the Internat-
ional Settlement and in Western Chapei. Sakamaki states that
Wang "ai An acted as liaison officer between him and the Chinese
Communist Party.

The information divulged by Sakamaki whilst in custody at
the Japanese Consulate has enabled the Japanese Consular Police
to effect the arrest of nineteen Japanese students of the Tung
Wen College, No.100 Hungjao Road, for communist activities.

In the dormitory of the Tung Wen College was found a
document addressed to Brother Yamamoto (Sakamaki), dealing with
the appointment of new members, presumably to the Japanese
Communist Party, and the spheres in which these were to direct
their energies etc.etc.

History of Sakamaki

Takashi Sakamaki alias Yamamoto was born at Uematsu-cho,
Nishishimagun, Nagano Prefecture, Japan. He attended the Kiso
Middle School in this prefecture and graduated in 1928. In April
of the latter year he arrived at Shanghai. After residing for two
months at the N.W. Kaisha Quarters in Gordon Road, where his
brother was employed, he returned to Nagano. For nearly a year he
remained with relatives in Japan. During April 1929 he came once
again to Shanghai and this time enrolled as a student at the
Tung Wen College on Hungjao Road. The following year it became
known that he was concerned in communist activities among the
students of the college and in December 1930 he was arrested
together with certain other students in connection with the

在这些逮捕行动发生几天后，从当地日本领事警察处收到情报，表明 Sakamaki 是由“第三舰队水兵会议青年部”发行的日文共产主义传单的作者。值得注意的是，最近在国际租界和闸北西区发现了多份此类传单的副本。Sakamaki 称，王乃安（Wang "ai An）充当了他与中国共产党之间的联络官。

Sakamaki 在日本领事馆被拘留期间泄露的情报，使日本领事警察得以逮捕虹桥路100号同文书院（Tung Wen College）的十九名日本学生，罪名是从事共产主义活动。

在同文书院的宿舍里，发现了一份写给山本兄弟（即 Sakamaki）的文件，内容涉及新成员的任命，推测是加入日本共产党，以及这些人应发挥作用的领域等等。

Sakamaki 生平

高志·坂卷（Takashi Sakamaki），又名山本，出生于日本长野县西岛郡上松町。他就读于该县木曾中学，并于1928年毕业。同年4月抵达上海。在戈登路西北公司（N.W. Kaisha）宿舍居住两个月后（其兄受雇于此），他返回长野。他在日本与亲戚住了近一年。1929年4月，他再次来到上海，这次注册成为虹桥路同文书院的学生。次年，据悉他参与了该院学生中的共产主义活动，1930年12月，他与其他一些学生因涉及

distribution of communistic pamphlets to a party of Japanese
naval cadets, who were visiting the college at the time. On
this occasion no charge was preferred against him by the
Japanese authorities.

It has now been definitely established that Sakamaki is
the chief of the Japanese Section of the Foreign Soldiers of
the Chinese Communist Party, of which he became a member in
May 1932.

The Third Fleet Sailors Conference was organised by him
and he planned forming a Shanghai branch of the Japanese
Communist Party, but this scheme failed to materialise.

Attached are translations of the pamphlets referred to
above.

Jai io（音译）提出的理论是，在印度……包裹着红宝石用于……在……旅馆，这意味着它们可以进入 J Tusex（音译）美元的所有权，并使用这家餐馆。

记录中另一起在水柴盒中发现共产主义材料的案例是由一名日本水手报告的，他声称于1月24日在日本军舰“luo i oosun”（音译，原文不清）的营区内捡到的一个火柴盒内发现了一份反动传单。

2月23日，工部局警务处的一名探员在闸北西部获得了一份日文共产主义传单。这本小册子由第三舰队水手会议青年部出版，敦促日本水兵要求加薪100%；要求被送回国，并向上述共产主义组织提供援助。

3月11日晚上7时30分，公共租界巡捕房根据日本总领事馆签发的搜查令，对广西路430号太平洋饭店（Tai Ping Yang Hotel）进行了突击搜查，并在52号房间逮捕了一名名为T. Sakamaki（别名Yamamoto）的日本共产党员，指控其违反日本《治安维持法》。被告经审讯后被移交给日本领事警察。当时在房间内发现的一名中国人，Palikao Tang Hai An（唐海安，音译），系西杜路（Rue de Seydou）115号水果摊的摊主，也被拘留。后者目前正依据拘留令被羁押，因为有理由相信他受雇担任日本共产党与中国共产党之间的联络官。

History of Sakamaki

Takashi Sakamaki alias Yamamoto was born at Uenatsu-cho,
Nishishima-mura, Nagano Prefecture, Japan. He attended the Kiso
Middle School in this prefecture and graduated in 1928. In April
of the latter year he arrived at Shanghai. After residing for two
months at the N.W. Kaisha Quarters in Gordon Road, where his
brother was employed, he returned to Nagano. For nearly a year he
remained with relatives in Japan. During April 1929 he came once
again to Shanghai and this time enrolled as a student at the
Tung Wen College on Hungjao Road. The following year it became
known that he was concerned in communist activities among the
students of the college and in December 1930 he was arrested
together with certain other students in connection with the

坂卷的历史

Takashi Sakamaki（别名Yamamoto）出生于日本长野县西岛村上夏町。他就读于该县的木曾中学，并于1928年毕业。同年4月，他抵达上海。在戈登路西北公司宿舍（其兄弟在此工作）居住两个月后，他返回长野。他在日本与亲戚待了将近一年。1929年4月，他再次来到上海，这次注册成为虹桥路同文学院的学生。次年，人们得知他参与了该院学生中的共产主义活动，1930年12月，他与其他一些学生因涉及

With reference to the attached report from D.S.

“1月20日，我从吴淞路441号宏源祥百货店（Hung Yuin Ziang General Store）购买了一包‘美利’牌火柴，内含十盒。我从包装中取出一盒火柴放入口袋（他出示了发现传单的火柴盒）。1月29日，我在该火柴盒内整齐折叠并隐藏在火柴下方的两份上述传单。在我家中使用的一盒火柴中，也以同样方式发现了一份类似的隐藏传单。我在家人的协助下，进一步搜索了于1月25日从上述商店购买的三包火柴，但未发现传单。我将两份小册子副本移交给了工部局警务处，一份移交给了日本餐厅工会办公室。”

The Shankaikwan Incident has become serious. Let
us oppose the massacre of Chinese labourers and farmers.
Dear Sailors, our brethren,

The Japanese Government of capitalists and landowners
which occupied Shankaikwan is attempting to make you kill
Chinese farmers and labourers in the Shanghai area.
The emergency call which started three days ago is
nothing but preparation for the massacre. Soon your
leave will be prohibited. Prepare yourselves discussing
with men of all squads and companies ways and means
to oppose this order. Do not kill the Chinese brethren.
Oppose the war of the capitalists and landowners. Submit
demands to officers. Let us join the Sailors Kyogikai.

The Third Fleet Sailors Kyogikai.

...............................

Dear Sailors,

Do not be deceived by such words as "For the sake of our
homeland" and "For our nationals". In our country our aged
parents are suffering from cold by being robbed of their
supporters. For whose sake are we staying in Shanghai? Do not
the landowners and capitalists squeeze our comrades, labourers
and tenant-farmers? We still continue to live a life of
slavery even in Shanghai. Our work is worse than that of miners.
If we make a slight mistake punishment will be freely imposed
on us in such a cruel manner as if dealt to animals. How can

and men. Oppose discriminating treatment between officers
and men.

to oppose the capitalists and landowners. We must therefore
unite ourselves firmly under the banner of the "Soldiers
Conference" in order to oppose officers.
